Andrew the Apostle
AN-droo thee uh-PAH-sul
noun
From Greek Andreas (G406, 'manly,' from anēr, a man); the brother of Simon Peter and one of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.

Biblical Definition

Andrew, whose name means manly, was the brother of Simon Peter and a fisherman of Bethsaida. He appears first as a disciple of John the Baptist, and when the Baptist pointed to Jesus and cried 'Behold the Lamb of God,' Andrew followed Christ and abode with Him that day (John 1:35-40). His very next act sets the pattern of his whole life: he first findeth his own brother Simon and brings him to Jesus, saying 'We have found the Messias' (John 1:41-42). Thus Peter, the great preacher of Pentecost, was brought to Christ by his quieter brother. Andrew is the apostle of bringing others to the Lord. It is Andrew who brings the lad with the five barley loaves and two small fishes to Jesus before the feeding of the five thousand (John 6:8-9), and Andrew with Philip who brings the inquiring Greeks to Christ (John 12:22). He was one of the four who heard the Olivet Discourse privately (Mark 13:3). Reformed teaching honors Andrew as a true minister of the Word in seed form, for evangelism is nothing more nor less than one sinner saying to another, come and see. His example rebukes the notion that only the prominent serve; the man who brought Peter is named with the twelve foundations of the church, an apostle of the Lamb whose labor the Lord sovereignly used to gather His elect.

Webster 1828 Definition

Simon Peter's brother, one of the first disciples called, the apostle who characteristically brings others to Christ.

ANDREW THE APOSTLE, noun. From Greek Andreas (G406, 'manly'); brother of Simon Peter and one of the twelve apostles.

A fisherman of Bethsaida, first a disciple of John the Baptist, who followed Jesus when the Baptist named Him the Lamb of God.

His first recorded act was to find his brother Simon and bring him to Christ.

As it is written, 'He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias' (John 1:41).

He brought the lad with the loaves and the inquiring Greeks to Jesus, the apostle of bringing others to the Lord.

Key Scripture

Joh 1:40 — "One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother."

Joh 1:41 — "He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ."

Mat 4:18 — "And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers."

Joh 6:8 — "One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, saith unto him,"

Modern Corruption

Andrew is sometimes eclipsed by his more prominent brother, obscuring the biblical truth that the Lord uses obscure servants to gather the great.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The danger here is not redefinition but neglect; Andrew is so overshadowed by Peter that his distinct calling is easily missed. Yet Scripture names him among the twelve foundations of the church, and his quiet ministry of bringing men to Christ is the very work to which every believer is called.

The principle to recover is that the Lord delights to use the unheralded. The man who brought Peter to Jesus did more for the church than many a louder voice, for evangelism is simply one sinner saying to another, come and see. Andrew teaches that faithfulness, not prominence, is the measure of a servant, and that God's sovereign grace often works through the brother no one remembers.

Hebrew Roots

Greek Andreas (G406), 'manly,' identifies the fisherman-apostle brother of Simon Peter.

expand to see more

Greek Andreas (G406) — Andrew, 'manly,' derived from anēr, a man

A native of Bethsaida and a fisherman by trade alongside his brother Simon

First a disciple of John the Baptist before following Christ as the Lamb of God

Named among the twelve apostles in every apostolic list (Matt 10:2; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:14)

Characterized by bringing others to Jesus: Simon, the lad with the loaves, the Greeks

Usage

"Andrew the apostle brought his brother Peter to Christ before Peter had spoken a word."

"Like Andrew, the humblest believer may say to another, We have found the Messias."

"The Lord used Andrew, the quieter brother, to gather the great preacher of Pentecost."
